keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria drops Surasena in -405, but the page has it last as a Magadhan acquisition (infobox 'Disestablished: c. 300 BCE', 'Magadha' as successor). Cliopatria's Shaishunaga shape for -404 holds none of Surasena's disc and the Nanda shape from -333 holds all of it, so the state is kept to -334 to leave no stateless gap; the page's c. 300 BCE would overlap the Nanda and Maurya shapes.

region.text: 'one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas (lit. 'great realms') in the 6th century BCE', capital Mathura

ledger.note: 600 BCE: Surasena enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the Yamuna at Mathura. The infobox gives 'Established: c. 700 BCE' and the page places the Mahajanapadas in 'the 6th century BCE'; -600 is Cliopatria's first year, so the year is a bridge.

334 BCE: Surasena passes to Magadha. The page is silent on any conquest, by the Nandas, the Mauryas or anyone; its infobox has 'Disestablished: c. 300 BCE' with Magadha as successor. -334 is the last year before Cliopatria's Nanda shape, which covers the Braj country, so the year is a bridge.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier at all for Surasena.

sources.title: Surasena
sources.note: Braj region, Mathura, infobox c. 700-c. 300 BCE, Avantiputta king of the Surasenas, Megasthenes' Sourasenoi; silent on conquests and boundaries.

notes: One page for two shapes, and the page is thin: it gives no boundary, no ruler list with dates and no conquest. Not settled: (1) the end: infobox c. 300 BCE (the same c. 700-c. 300 BCE infobox dates as the Vatsa page) against Cliopatria's Nanda shape covering the country from -333; -334 is a confidence-1 bridge, and the Nanda dossier should list the gain. (2) 'Avantiputta, the king of the Surasenas' is mentioned in Buddhist texts 'in the time of Maha Kachchana' but the page describes no political relation with Avanti, and Matsya, Kuru and Panchala are not mentioned. (3) Painted Grey Ware (1100-500 BCE) and Northern Black Polished Ware (700-200 BCE) phases at Mathura and a Saurasena coin dated 400-300 BCE are the page's only dated evidence. (4) My Mathura radius overlaps the Matsya correction by about 1,500 km2 on the west; both are guesses at a boundary the pages do not draw. (5) No wars listed.
